Retrieved 2026-07-19 via Exa. Independent + Guardian + FT + BBC all published 2026-07-18 ~20:00 BST.

Burnham to scrap Starmer's £2bn digital ID scheme.
- Burnham will scrap Keir Starmer's digital ID programme when he takes office Monday, in a "reset of priorities" — his first major policy break with Starmer confirmed before becoming PM.
- Scheme cost put at £2bn (Independent). Money earmarked redirected to "tangible" improvements / cost of living.
- Starmer announced digital ID at last year's Labour conference; mandatory for right-to-work checks as illegal-immigration crackdown; later watered down to voluntary after backlash. Petition against attracted ~3m signatures.
- Burnham spokesperson: "One of the first things this government will do is put its focus where people need it right now: creating breathing space and delivering change they can feel in their everyday lives. That means all the time and resource that was going to be spent on a national ID scheme will go instead to where it's most needed, such as helping with the cost of living. This government is determined to bring power back to communities, instead of hoarding it in Whitehall. We will work every day to lift this country back up to where it belongs - with growth in every postcode, and hope in every heart."
- Also reported (Independent): Burnham plans to scrap reforms watering down right to jury trial, and restore rebel MP Karl Turner to the parliamentary party after suspension.
- Guardian: "reset of priorities"; resources reallocated to cost of living; team indicated on Saturday.
